newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-HENDRY LEVEL WITH WILLIAMS, O'SULLIVAN LEADS.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-HENDRY LEVEL WITH WILLIAMS, O'SULLIVAN LEADS.

text.p: Titleholder Stephen Hendry was locked in an 8-8 stalemate with Welsh pretender Mark Williams after the second session of their best-of-25-frame second round match in the world championship on Friday.

Englishman Ronnie O'Sullivan, meanwhile, snatched the last two frames to take a 9-7 lead over Darren Morgan and stay on course for a quarter-final against Hendry if both come through their matches on Saturday.
The first session between the champion and Williams, who whipped him 9-2 in the British Open final this month, ended 4-4 with Hendry fortunate to be level.
Williams, a superb potter, led 4-1 with chances to move further ahead as Hendry made unaccustomed errors. But he could not capitalise.
In the evening he opened leads of 6-4 and 8-6, only to be pegged back to level both times .
Williams will look upon opportunities squandered against the off-form champion, whose highest break on the day was only 59.

O'Sullivan, the 21-year-old eighth seed who made a perfect 147 in the first round, was fortunate to lead Morgan, a dour Welshman who had chances in the last two frames and who can count himself unlucky to be trailing.
The exciting Englishman needs to win just four more frames when the best-of-25-frame match resumes on Saturday morning to set up the possible clash with Hendry.
In another second round match, Canadian 14th seed Alain Robidoux lead 5-3 against England's Stefan Mazrocis, who upset third seed Peter Ebdon in the first round.
